jobs.occupation: Start your career as an Audit Graduate at Deloitte Copenhagen 2027
jobs.description:
Company Description

With more than 2700 employees Deloitte is the largest audit and consultancy firm in Denmark. We tailor solutions across Audit, Tax, Financial Advisory Services, Enterprise Risk Services, and Consulting.

Would you like to start your audit career at Deloitte's head office?

At our Copenhagen office you will get 600 Audit & Assurance colleagues across departments. We have a strong sense of community, with many joint events, from Friday bars to courses and development opportunities. This gives you plenty of opportunity to build a strong network and a foundation for where your career at Deloitte will take you.

Job Description

As an audit graduate, your day-to-day work will take place in either our Portfolio or Large & Complex departments. You will be assigned to one of our four client segments: Public, Private, Financial Services, or Top Tier and your daily work will be team-based. You will have a dedicated department manager and a coach to support your personal and professional development.

You will quickly become part of your new community and have ample opportunity to build new relationships.

As an audit graduate you:

• Always work in audit teams and be in close contact with both colleagues and clients - often working on site at the client's premises.

• Acquire extensive knowledge of your department's clients and, most importantly, the skills to advise and audit them.

• Assist in planning client's audits, coordinating efforts with, for example, Deloitte's Service and Delivery Centres, which handle many of our administrative tasks, ahead of the reporting season.

• Contribute to risk assessments of accounting areas, using your knowledge of the client's internal processes.

• Work with an experienced audit team to conduct audits to ensure that the financial statements give a true and fair view.

Your role will vary depending on which department you join but we promise that your days will not be the same. There will be room to learn, to ask for help, and to grow and take on the responsibility you want.

NEXT - our graduate development programme

When you join as an audit graduate, you enter a full-time role and will join our internal development programme, NEXT, along with around 100 other graduates across the country. You are regularly brought together for training and to prepare for new roles.

Depending on where you are in your training when you join us, you will also be studying part-time at the university. And for your first 100 days with us, you will be assigned a buddy who has been through the experience of being a new graduate and will help you settle into your new role.

Qualifications

There are several paths to become an audit graduate in our audit business. We are open to your educational background and to you completing a level of training while you are with us. The most important thing is that you have the interest and motivation to learn. And it is important that you:

• Want to develop personally.

• Are curious about auditing.

• Have social skills that will support your future relationships with clients and colleagues, and team-based working.

• Can show relevant professional experience or extra curricular activities , in which you have excelled.

• You speak and understand both English and Danish, or any of the other Nordic languages.

• You are eligible to work within the EU, either as a citizen or with the correct permits.

At Deloitte, we value different skills, perspectives, and experiences, as it enables us to effectively solve complex challenges for our clients. We encourage you to apply for the position if you believe your skills can contribute to our team´s success.

Even if you do not see yourself in all the bullets above, we still encourage you to apply if you believe your skills can make an impact on our team.

Additional Information

Click on "I am interested" above to apply for this position.

Please attach your CV and grades from your current and previous education. Please do not upload a traditional cover letter. Through the application process we will also ask you to answer a few questions about your motivation for the joining Deloitte.

We process applications and arrange interviews continually.

Expected start date to be 10.09.2027.

If you have any questions about the position or the recruitment process, please contact Recruitment Coordinator Emil Morelli Nørgaard on mobile: +45 53793260 or email: talent@deloitte.dk

We encourage all candidates to apply for the position regardless of, e.g., age, gender (gender identity and gender expression), sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity, nationality, or disability.

We look forward to hearing from you!

In Deloitte, you will find passionate, caring people who are curious by nature and striving to evolve. We value our different skills, perspectives and experiences and foster an environment where innovative powers thrive. To us, success is the feeling that the work we are doing will outlast us. The impact we make is not about what we achieve as individuals, but how we enable those around us to be their very best. From professional development to leadership opportunities, we empower our people to be extraordinary by playing to their strengths – because that is how we can make a difference.

Company Description

With more than 2,700 employees, Deloitte is the largest audit and consultancy firm in Denmark. We tailor solutions across Audit, Tax, Financial Advisory Services, Enterprise Risk Services, Technology, and Transformations.

About our team

Finance Transformation is part of Deloitte’s consulting practice and consists of 350 dedicated consultants who work within all aspects of the CFO area and engage with clients to advise, transform, optimize, and operate the finance function. We have private and public as well as national and international clients across different industries and of different sizes, and we work with the lion’s share of C25 companies and public institutions.

Global Business Services (GBS) is an integral part of Deloitte’s Finance Transformation practice. The GBS team is dedicated to helping organizations transform their business operations, driving higher efficiency, effectiveness, and agility. By leveraging a comprehensive suite of services, the GBS practice supports clients in optimizing shared services, outsourcing, and global business service models to create value and enhance performance. We work in the full lifecycle of projects from strategy to design and implementation.

We are seeking an experienced and skilled Manager to join our Global Business Services (GBS) team. The ideal candidate has experience in setting up shared services organizations and a deep understanding of multi-functional GBS operations. Experience with the interplay of technology and process design in this context is preferred. This role will be pivotal in driving strategic business transformation initiatives, building effective governance structures, implementing new capabilities globally and optimizing functional processes leveraging the latest technologies.

Job Description

As a GBS Strategy Manager, you will lead large complex engagements for some of the world's biggest organizations. In this role, you will architect future-ready GBS strategies, drive end-to-end finance process transformations, and leverage cutting-edge AI technologies to enable growth and value creation. You will be responsible for leading business model transformations, setting up shared services or outsourcing solutions, and leveraging a commercial mindset to position and scale innovation. You will identify, design, and implement shared services solutions aimed at driving operational effectiveness, cost efficiencies, and organizational agility.

In this role, you will make an impact by:

• Identifying key client business issues and architecting end-to-end finance process transformations (e.g., R2R, O2C, P2P)

• Driving business development by responding to Requests for Proposal (RFPs) and pitching strategic solutions with a strong commercial mindset

• Evaluating and deploying innovative technologies, including GenAI and intelligent automation, to elevate client digital maturity and process performance

• Determining which techniques, delivery models, and emerging tech are best suited to serving each client's unique addressable needs

• Developing recommendations for the client in the context of overall engagement

• Leading day-to-day team activities and effectively overseeing the quality of deliverables

• Managing diverse small and big teams

Qualifications

Ideally, you have:

• Around 6-9 years of relevant experience in the GBS, Shared Services and/or Business Process Outsourcing, as well as good understanding of finance processes

• 3+ years of Direct people management experience

• Bachelor's degree from an accredited university

• Fluency in Danish is a big plus

What you bring to the team:

• Experience with multiple GBS pillars including, but not limited to HR, IT, Finance, Procurement, Commercial Operations, Legal

• Extensive project experience within the Shared Services, Outsourcing and/or Offshoring industry, or back-office functional optimization

• Experience with service delivery model strategy, design, implementation & optimization for multi-functional or single-function entities

• Strong critical thinking, analytical and problem-solving skills

• Exceptional interpersonal, team-building and oral and written communication skills; outstanding integrity, initiative, creativity, and passion

• Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, ambiguous, dynamic environment and manage multiple priorities.

Even if you do not see yourself in all the bullets above, we still encourage you to apply if you believe your skills can make an impact on our team.

Click the "I am interested" button above if you are ready to join our team.

Send your CV by 30.11.2026. We process applications and arrange interviews continually, so we recommend that you apply as soon as possible.

Expected start date: Flexible

Please do not hesitate to contact Nadiia Novikova at nshamarina@deloitte.dk if you have any questions about the position.

jobs.occupation: Computational and Data Staff Scientist Novo Nordisk Foundation Center for Protein Design
jobs.description:
We seek an experienced, highly motivated, and independent computational and data scientist to support the Novo Nordisk Foundation Center for Protein Design (CPD), University of Copenhagen (UCPH). The post suits someone with experience in computational chemistry, biology, and/or structural biology, as well as managing big data. This is a full-time position, starting 1 February 2027 and employment through 31 July 2032.

  Our research
 The CPD is a new initiative at UCPH. It is a multidisciplinary centre that works across the university—notably with the Departments of Biology, Drug Design and Pharmacology, Chemistry, and Computer Science—and with national and international academic and industrial partners. CPD is funded by an initial grant of 700M DKK for seven years from the Novo Nordisk Foundation. At capacity, the CPD is expected to have ≈8 research groups, ≈80 researchers, and support staff. Research will encompass the growing protein design landscape with computational, experimental, applied and hybrid projects.

  The CPD's vision and mission are to accelerate protein design by deepening understanding of sequence-to-structure/function relationships in proteins, and to train the next generation of protein scientists to apply protein-design approaches and methods to a diverse array of fundamental and real-world challenges.  

  CPD research is broadly organised into three themes: Programmable De Novo Protein Design, aimed at improving methods for protein design by combining rational, physics-based and AI-based approaches; Contextualised Protein Design, that is, designing proteins that are fit for purpose such as working directly and optimally in cells, chemical reactors, etc; and Biodesign for Sustainability and Healthcare, for instance working with biotech and industry to deliver synthetic proteins to address grand challenges in these areas.

  Data science at CPD: Increasingly, modern protein science is about data: collecting it, organising it, analysing it, and learning from it to build a deeper understanding of how proteins fold and function. Protein design is no different. Indeed, through the application of generative AI, it is at the leading edge of the confluence of data science and protein science. To coordinate this in the CPD, we are looking for someone experienced in and excited about working at this interface.

  Further information on the CPD see: cpd.ku.dk.

  Learn more about the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, https://drug.ku.dk/

  Your job
 Specifically, we seek a talented computational and data scientist and team player to help develop research infrastructure, including hardware and computational tools, to advance the CPD’s research and mission. The successful candidate will join a growing multidisciplinary team to help collect, organise, analyse, and exploit data from computationally designed protein sequences and structural models, through protein expression levels, and onto a wide range of experimental structure-function studies. A key part of the role will be integrating into the wider team and working collaboratively with CPD researchers, rather than simply providing a data-management service. For example, we anticipate that the successful candidate would assist with and lead on various projects with CPD researchers to develop robust, reliable, and scalable data and computational tools to enable the very best protein design.

  Key responsibilities will include

   	
• Helping establish CPD's computational infrastructure to provide computing and data management for its researchers 	
• Developing automated pipelines that convert raw instrument output files directly into data plots suitable for analysis, saving time and resources across the research pipeline 	
• Collecting data and generating databases of designed proteins, e.g., constructs, sequences, models, and biophysical data (LIMS) 	
• Assisting in the development of new predictive models based on the gathered experimental and computational data using machine learning methods 	
• Being responsible for data management plans at the CPD and coordinating these plans with the host departments 	
• Related to the above, managing (i.e., best practice in collecting, organising, accessing) data generated by computational protein design workflows and by the CPD’s Protein Biophysics Facility 	
• Advising and training CPD scientists in creating and analysing large computational datasets, linking their experimental data and computational data to extract key information, and managing their computational protein design pipelines 	
• Contributing to, and where appropriate leading, grant applications for and publications from CPD research projects 	
• Teaching appropriate aspects of the above on CPD Master’s and PhD courses 	
• Serving as the primary technical bridge between the CPD and central KU IT to set up CPD’s computing systems in close collaboration with KU IT and establish internal data processing environments   Qualifications and expectations
 To succeed in this role, we anticipate that your areas of expertise could include one or more of the following:

   	
• Computational protein modelling and, ideally, design 	
• Protein or biomolecular sequence data and analysis 	
• Collection, manipulation and use of data from protein biophysics and structural biology 	
• Use and understanding of modern biomolecular statistical data analysis, including ML and AI methods, and generative AI for protein modelling and design 	
• Experience of establishing computational infrastructures for the above   Essential experience and skills

   	
• A PhD in bioinformatics, data science or a related domain, e.g. computational/structural biology 	
• Excellent knowledge of scientific computing and coding languages, e.g., Python 	
• Documented experience (e.g., scientific publications) in machine learning, scientific computing, and similar 	
• An active interest in protein design, engineering, and structure  	
• A proven ability to work with others on challenging multidisciplinary problems 	
• A team player keen on collaborating with researchers from different backgrounds and who is service-minded with clear organisational, communication, and networking skills. 	
• Excellent skills in written and spoken English   Desirable experience and skills

   	
• Knowledge of experimental protein science, for example, biophysical methods and/or structural biology 	
• Experience in computational molecular/structural biology   Place of employment
 The place of employment is at the NNF Center for Protein Design, located at the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, University of Copenhagen. We offer creative, stimulating working conditions in a dynamic, international research environment.

  Salary and terms of employment
 The employment is a full-time (37 hours/week) position with a fixed-term until 31 July 2032. The starting date will be 1 February 2027.

  Depending on qualifications the position will take place as Special Consultant or Senior Consultant in accordance with the Circular on the Collective Agreement concerning Academics in the state sector concluded between the Danish Ministry of Finance and Akademikerne (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations). There will be an opportunity to negotiate supplements based on qualifications. The monthly salary will be based on the number of years of work experience (seniority), with the possibility to negotiate a salary supplement based on prior experience and qualifications. The employer will pay an additional 18.07 % to your pension fund.
 You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  Questions
 For further information regarding the position, please contact Center Manager Gretchen Repasky, Gretchen.repasky@bio.ku.dk.

  Application
 Your application should be in English and include:

   	
• A cover letter outlining your fit to the role and motivation for applying (max. one page). 	
• Curriculum Vitae (incl. the names of two referees) (max. two pages)  	
• List of publications including preprints (no limit, but do not include copies of the papers) 	
• A certified/signed copy of certificate(s) of education   Please submit your application by clicking on “Apply Now” below.

  Application deadline: 8 November 2026

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not meet the above requirements.

  The University wishes to reflect the diversity of the surrounding society and encourages all qualified candidates, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position.

Rich in tradition and modern in outlook, the University gives students and staff the opportunity to cultivate their talent in an ambitious and informal environment. To accomplish our goal of being the best at what we do, we are focused on building a world-class ML engineering workflow, ensuring seamless training, deployment and monitoring of our predictive models.

• A modern office in Copenhagen (Nordhavn) with a flexible hybrid work model.

• A flat hierarchy with high levels of trust, autonomy, and freedom to make decisions.

• A valued role with unique responsibilities and plenty of room for creativity.

A three-year position as a Postdoctoral researcher is now available at the Copenhagen Health Complexity Center, Department of Public Health, University of Copenhagen. The Postdoc’s employment is expected to start on 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  About the Center

  You will be employed at the Copenhagen Health Complexity Center, which aims to build a strong scientific foundation for understanding and acting on complex public-health challenges. The Center leverages multi-layered nationwide social and health data combined with an interdisciplinary fusion of methods spanning data science, epidemiology, ethnography, econometrics, and systems science. Our research focuses on the complex interplay of health, social, and environmental factors that shape individuals, families, and networks over time. We emphasise interdisciplinary collaboration, offering you an opportunity to actively engage as a collaborative partner in different projects depending on your interests and expertise. Learn more about the Center and our research, vision, and values here.

  About the Department 

  The Department of Public Health provides the scientific foundation for researchers and educators who aim to improve public health, both nationally and globally, and to create greater insight into the links between health, the individual, and society as well as the ethical, equity, and political implications. This is achieved through research, education, and engagement with stakeholders and the general public along with a broad multidisciplinary research agenda that addresses most aspects of public health at a high international level. More information about the Department of Public Health is available here.

  About the position 

  The position will be nested within the Child Health group at the Center, where we advance knowledge through a combination of research activities that leverage the Center’s data infrastructures and methodological expertise, and engagement with policymakers and practitioners. The Center has developed a strategic partnership with a Danish municipality – the Thriving Communities Lab – which offers a platform for connecting the scientific activities at the Center with real-world health promotion efforts. The focus of this partnership is to enhance the conditions for adolescents to thrive through a dynamic learning process that involves professionals across sectors in the municipality, the local government, and researchers, over a period of several years. One question we will explore is whether computational modelling can usefully bring together local knowledge, scientific evidence, the Center’s data resources, and insights emerging from practical interventions, and so strengthen this learning process. Your work as a postdoc will be anchored around this question. Our vision at the Center is to build on this experience to engage with more municipalities over time, addressing a variety of complex health challenges.

  As a Postdoc, your responsibilities will primarily consist of: 

   	
• Spearheading the development of a decision-support/scenario exploration tool that offers policymakers a way to visualize and simulate systemic effects of social investments and programmes, in close collaboration with our partners in the Thriving Communities Lab. 	
• Engaging with municipal collaborators within the Thriving Communities Lab to ensure a dynamic interplay between research activities and local efforts. 	
• Exploring multi-layered life-course data from the Danish Life Course Cohort (DANLIFE), augmented with local data from the municipal partner, to map the interrelated landscape of well-being among adolescents. 	
• Contributing to scientific publications and engage in the dissemination of research results related to these topics. 	
• Collaborating with researchers in the Center on interdisciplinary projects. 	
• Participating in research-based teaching at the Department of Public Health. 	
• Actively contributing to the development of organisational elements within the Center, such as network activities, website, outreach initiatives, social engagements, scientific meetings, and more.   Profile 

  We are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic researcher with the following competences and experience:

   	
• You have a PhD degree in social science, economics, epidemiology, data science, complexity science, computational science, or other related sciences. 	
• You have experience with system dynamics modelling. Experience with agent-based modelling, social return on investment analysis or other analytical frameworks to model social and systemic impacts of social policies and programmes would also be an advantage. 	
• Experience working with Danish register data is an advantage. 	
• You are motivated to engage in participatory processes with practitioners and policymakers, and to collaborate with a variety of stakeholders to foster change. 	
• You have an active interest in complex-systems science applied to public health and epidemiology. 	
• You have proficient communication skills and a proven ability to work in interdisciplinary teams. 	
• You have excellent English skills, both written and spoken. 	
• Danish language skills are an advantage but not essential.   Place of employment

  The place of employment is the Copenhagen Health Complexity Center, Department of Public Health, University of Copenhagen, next to the Lakes in Central Copenhagen.

  Terms of employment 
 The average working hours are 37 hours per week. The position is a fixed-term position limited to a period of 3 years. The start date is February 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. Salary, pension and other conditions of employment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or another relevant organisation. Currently, the monthly salary starts at 35,000 DKK/approx. 4,700 EUR (October 2021 level). Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 17.1 % to your pension fund. Foreign and Danish applicants may be eligible for tax reductions if they hold a PhD degree and have not lived in Denmark for the past 10 years. The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2020.

  Further information

  For specific information about the position, please contact the Associate professor Christopher Jamil de Montgomery: cmon@sund.ku.dk

  Applicants may find the following links useful:

   	
• Copenhagen Health Complexity Center: https://healthcomplex.dk/ 	
• University of Copenhagen: http://ku.dk/english/ 	
• Department of Public Health: http://publichealth.ku.dk/ 	
• International Staff Mobility: https://ism.ku.dk/   Application process

  Your application should be written in English and must include the following documents – all in PDF format:

   	
• Letter of motivation (max 1 page). Please briefly describe your previous research experience and interests as well as what attracts you to the position. 	
• Curriculum Vitae, including a list of publications. 	
• Certified/signed copies of
 	a) PhD certificate (if the PhD has not been completed, a written statement from the applicant’s supervisor will suffice)
 	b) Master of Science certificate. 	
• A research plan (max 2 pages) outlining your ideas for how a decision-support/scenario exploration tool could be developed, drawing on system dynamics modelling or other analytical frameworks suitable for modelling dynamic effects of social policies and programmes.   Please submit your application by clicking on “Apply Now” below. Only online applications will be considered.

  After the expiration of the deadline for applications, the authorised recruitment manager will select applicants for assessment based on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been advanced for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment has been completed, each applicant is given an opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant themselves.

  You can read more about the recruitment process here: https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  Application deadline 

  Deadline for applications: 31/10/2026 23.59pm CET 

  We reserve the right to reject material received after the deadline, and to reject applications that do not meet the abovementioned requirements.

  Interviews are expected to be held in week 47-48.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the diversity of society and encourages all qualified candidates to apply regardless of their personal background.

Can you own the platform and pipelines that EIVA’s software is built on?

EIVA is an equipment and software engineering company delivering solutions to the international maritime industry. Our customers operate within renewable energy, oil & gas exploration, seabed-to-surface construction and hydrographic surveying – often in demanding environments where timing, precision and safety margins matter.

You do not need to know the subsea domain to apply. Here, your product is the software itself, and your users are the other engineering teams who build and ship on the platform you own. What matters is curiosity – the ability to ask the right questions and translate what you hear into good technical decisions – and a collaborative, team-first mindset.

The position is based at EIVA’s Danish office in Stilling (just one minute from the E45, approximately 15 minutes from Aarhus by car and easily accessible by bus).

What's involved?

As Tech Lead – Infrastructure, you'll own the platform, pipelines and infrastructure that our NaviSuite software is built on.

Around 80% of the role is hands-on: working directly in the team's technical domains – platform, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure as code, environments and tooling. The rest is technical leadership – owning architecture within the Infrastructure team, making the final call on anything inside the team's decision domain, and knowing when a question needs to go further, to our architects or to alignment with other teams. You'll also help keep that decision domain itself well defined: what the team can decide on its own, and where it needs external alignment.

There could be occasional travel – around one to two short trips a year.

Your responsibilities…

• Doing hands-on development and engineering work across the team's core technical domains – platform, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure as code, environments and internal tooling (around 80% of the role)

• Making the final technical decisions within the team's decision domain, and helping define where that domain's boundaries sit versus where the team needs external alignment

• Securing technical quality in the team – code and infrastructure-as-code review, best practices, testing and automation standards

• Owning architecture in the team – ensuring platform and pipeline work aligns with EIVA's overall architecture, and explaining the interdependencies to the team

• Participating in refinement, securing that features, stories and tasks describe architectural dependencies, feasibility, quality requirements and operational aspects such as reliability, security, cost and developer experience

• Cross team alignment – representing the Infrastructure team's technical position and making sure its work fits with adjacent work elsewhere in the organisation

• Driving clarification with architects on technical questions that sit outside the team's decision domain

Also part of the role…

• Providing technical mentoring and sparring for the team's engineers

• Supporting the other development teams as users of the platform – helping with adoption, guidance and acting on their feedback

• Taking operational responsibility for the platform and pipelines

• Keeping the team's technical practices current – seeking out training, evaluating new tooling and sharing that knowledge internally

• Maintaining technical documentation for the platform, pipelines and environments

• Giving technical input to hiring and onboarding new engineers on the team

• Giving technical input to estimation and planning together with the Team Manager/Product Owner

The ideal candidate…

• Has a background in software engineering or computer science

• Has hands-on experience building and maintaining platforms, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure as code and internal tooling

• Has experience managing complex DevOps systems and workflows, and is comfortable making final technical calls within a defined decision domain

• Is familiar with tools such as Git/GitHub, artifact storage, Ansible and Terraform

• Has a collaborative mindset – comfortable gathering feedback from stakeholders across teams and using it to design clean, well-reasoned solutions

• Is a team player who's good at knowledge-sharing and educating peers, and takes proactive ownership of their domain

• It's a bonus if you also have experience with licence management systems, but not a requirement.
